citations.title: Rules and Regulations for Assisted Living Communities (rule index .01-.34)
citations.requirement: Minimum standards for personal care homes licensed as assisted living communities (ALC, 25+ residents). The Secretary of State page and Cornell index list rules .01-.34, including .08 Community Leadership, .09 Workforce, .14 Emergency Preparedness, .19 Memory Care, .20 Medications, .26 Change in Condition, .29 Discharge and .30 Reports.

citations.title: Personal Care Homes (rules .01-.09 text retrieved)
citations.requirement: Governs personal care homes (2+ unrelated adults). Legal authority is O.C.G.A. Title 31, Chapters 2 and 7. A PCH may not provide assisted living care unless it holds an ALC license. The rules are mirrored for PCHs in the Secretary of State text; only .01-.06 were read in full here.

citations.title: Definitions
citations.requirement: Defines the terms the policies must use. Examples: abuse; injury (includes pressure ulcers not properly cared for); assistive device (needs a physician/NP/PA order, a written care plan and resident consent); assisted self-preservation; chemical and physical restraints (bedrails, wheelchair safety bars, tight tucking and mitts count; alarm wristbands do not); limited nursing services (care completed within 7 days or intermittently); memory care center; medical alert system (DCH-approved); proxy caregiver; Mattie's-call-related elopement; owner (10% or more interest).

citations.title: Application for Permit
citations.requirement: The governing body applies on DCH forms. DCH will not act on an incomplete application or one without fees (per Ch. 111-8-25). Required: floor plan with window, door, common-area and room measurements plus .jpg photos; administrator or on-site manager name; full ownership disclosure (10%+ owners and registered agent); ownership or lease documentation; local zoning addressed with local officials; initial application must include a CPA financial stability affidavit (going concern for 2 years).

citations.title: Permits
citations.requirement: Valid permit required before admitting residents. Permit displayed conspicuously where residents and visitors see it. Not transferable. Must be returned and is no longer valid if the community moves to an unlicensed location, ownership changes, or the permit is suspended or revoked. Separate permit for each premises. May not exceed licensed capacity on the permit face. Must disclose ALC licensure classification in marketing. No other business may operate on the premises in a way that intrudes on residents' quiet enjoyment.

citations.title: Owner Governance
citations.requirement: The community must have a functioning governing body that oversees compliance with Ch. 111-8-63, 111-8-25 and 111-8-100. The governing body implements policies supporting dignity, respect, choice, independence and privacy. Policies must at minimum direct staff and residents on: (a) services available, including memory care and proxy caregivers; (b) a staffing plan under which ratios rise as assisted-self-preservation residents increase; (c) admissions, discharges and immediate transfers that avoid admitting or retaining residents needing more care than the community is authorized or able to provide; (d) refunds on transfer or discharge; (e) staff training and evaluation; (f) house rules and enforcement; plus further items through investigation and reporting (list truncated in retrieved text; read the full paragraph before finalizing).

citations.title: Community Leadership
citations.requirement: Rule number and title confirmed from the official index (administrator and leadership requirements). Body text was NOT retrieved; confirm the content before citing paragraph numbers.

citations.title: Workforce Qualifications, Training and Staffing (amended eff. May 21, 2025)
citations.requirement: Full text read. (1) On-site manager and responsible staff 21+; no staff under 18 without line-of-sight supervision (17-year-old exception for a GA high-school nursing-assistant track). (2) All-staff training within 60 days. (3) Hands-on staff training within 60 days, including first aid and CPR with return demonstration. (4) At least 2 trained staff present at all times, one per occupied floor. (5) 24 CE hours in year one; (6) 16 hours annually after. (7) Training records. (10) TB screening and physical within 12 months before providing care. (11)-(13) Criminal background checks under Ch. 111-8-12. (14)-(15) Employment history; personnel files kept 3 years after departure. (17) No impairment on duty. (18) Average monthly ratio 1:15 awake waking hours and 1:20 non-waking for minimal-need residents; at least 2 direct care staff 24/7, one per occupied floor; RN or LPN on site 8 h/wk (1-30 residents), 16 (31-60), 24 (61-90), 40 (90+). (19) Sufficient staff time. (21) Staffing plans and schedules kept 1 year. (22) ID badges. (23) Medical alert system requirements.

citations.title: Community Accountability
citations.requirement: Records available to DCH inspectors. Inspection report disputes due within 10 days of receipt. Written plan of correction due within 10 days, with date-certain actions. Most recent inspection report and plan of correction displayed where residents and visitors see them. Website link to the previous 18 months of reports and plans if the community has a website. Keep an accurate licensed residential care profile. Services and marketing must match the license, profile and rules. Only a licensed ALC may hold itself out as offering assisted living care. No memory care center without a current certificate.

citations.title: Community Design and Use Requirements
citations.requirement: Rule number and title confirmed from the official index (physical plant). Body text NOT retrieved.

citations.title: Community Furnishings
citations.requirement: Furnishings maintained intact and functional. Name plate outside each resident's room unless declined. Closet or wardrobe and reading-adequate lighting in each room. Individual bed at least 36 x 72 inches with mattress at least 5 inches thick (4 if synthetic). No cots, roll-aways, double-decks, stacked bunks, hide-a-beds or studio couches in lieu of beds. Linens for residents needing linen service: at minimum 2 sheets, pillow, pillowcase, blanket, bedspread, towels and washcloth. Help hanging pictures. (Only some paragraphs were visible in the retrieved text.)

citations.title: Community Safety Precautions
citations.requirement: Interior and exterior kept clean, in good repair and free of unsafe conditions. Entrances, exits, sidewalks and escape routes kept free of hazards. Name and house number visible from the street. (Only (1), (11) and (12) were visible; fire drill and other paragraphs were not retrieved.)

citations.title: Emergency Preparedness
citations.requirement: Comply with Ch. 111-8-16 (Disaster Preparedness Plans). Post evacuation maps with marked escape routes on each floor. Keep a clear accessible emergency route through common areas. The disaster plan is readily accessible to staff, residents and families and names the staff positions responsible for implementing it and obtaining emergency medical attention. Give timely notice of the relocation address to residents, family contacts, representatives and DCH if an emergency forces relocation.

citations.title: Admission and Resident Retention
citations.requirement: (1) Admission profile: age 18+; no active TB; no need for continuous medical or nursing care; no need for physical or chemical restraints, isolation or confinement for behavioral control; able to actively participate in transfers; able to participate in social and leisure activities. (2) The administrator or on-site manager must document the evaluation of applicants, including a National Sex Offender Registry inquiry or fingerprint check and documented added safety measures for registered sex offenders or violent offenders. A physician examination on DCH forms is referenced. (4) Community admission decisions (text truncated in retrieved copy).

citations.title: Admission Agreements
citations.requirement: Plain-language agreement consistent with the licensed residential care profile. Must state all fees and what they cover. Written notice at least 30 days before any increase in personal-service charges and at least 60 days before any increase in room-and-board charges. Provisions for continuous assessment and referral or transfer on change of condition. A description of the complaint process. Transportation provisions, with emergency transport available at all times. A refund policy on death, transfer or discharge. Further items follow (truncated in retrieved text).

citations.title: Services in the Community
citations.requirement: (1) Provide assisted living including protective care and watchful oversight. (2) Resident needs assessment covering family supports, ADL function, physical care, medical information, cognitive and behavioral impairments and preferences. (3) Written care plan within 14 days of admission, updated at least annually and when needs change substantially or on assignment to a memory care center. (4) Daily social activities. (6) Operable non-pay telephone for staff emergency use and private resident access. (7) Do not restrict free access to common areas or lock a resident into or out of the bedroom. (8) Proxy caregiver options. (11) Periodic or short-term medical and nursing health services are not provided as community services; they are purchased by the resident (care planning, training, medication administration and competency checks excepted).

citations.title: Precautions for Residents at Risk of Elopement
citations.requirement: Rule number and title confirmed from the official index. Body text NOT retrieved; read before writing elopement-risk procedures.

citations.title: Additional Requirements for Certified Memory Care Centers
citations.requirement: Applies if the community holds itself out as providing specialized dementia care or charges more for it. The licensed residential care profile must carry a written description with 12 elements (philosophy, how services differ, staffing and training, admission and screening criteria, assessment and reassessment triggers before the customary quarterly review, staffing patterns, physical environment and security, activities, fees, discharge criteria, emergency procedures, family involvement). Staffing: one dementia-trained direct care staff per 12 residents in waking hours and per 15 in non-waking hours (monthly average). RN or LPN hours in the center: 8 h/wk (1-12 residents), 16 (13-30), 24 (31-40), 40 (more than 40). Annual staff training. Physical design paragraph (b) not read.

citations.title: Medications
citations.requirement: Full text read. Residents capable of self-administration may keep and self-administer medications securely. Staff assistance is limited to listed tasks for unit or multi-dose packaged medications, including EpiPen use under a written protocol with a 911 call. Only certified medication aides (CMAs) may administer. The community must check the Georgia Certified Medication Aide Registry, run skills competency checks, use an RN or pharmacist for quarterly random observations, and have a pharmacist do quarterly drug regimen reviews. An RN, pharmacist or physician does annual competency reviews. Orders are required for all medications including OTC. New prescriptions within 48 hours and MAR updated within 48 hours. Daily MAR. Medications stored under lock and key; controlled substances in a locked cabinet or box of substantial construction with a daily-updated log; duplicate keys on site; original containers; disposal per FDA/EPA guidance; liquid morphine limited to 50 ml per hospice patient.

citations.title: Nutrition and Food Preparation
citations.requirement: At least 3 regularly scheduled well-balanced meals per day, 7 days a week, plus therapeutic diets as ordered by the resident's healthcare provider. No more than 14 hours between the evening and morning meals. Nutrition per Recommended Daily Diet Allowances. At least one nutritious snack offered daily. Food must be clean, wholesome and safe. Menus dated and planned at least 1 week ahead for regular and therapeutic diets, posted or easily available, with resident input encouraged. Perishables held at or below 41 degrees F. A third-party reproduction states menus as served are kept 30 days. Only some paragraphs were visible.

citations.title: Temperature Control
citations.requirement: Rule number and title confirmed from the official index. Body text NOT retrieved (indoor temperature standards).

citations.title: Infection Control, Sanitation and Supplies
citations.requirement: Rule number and title confirmed from the official index. Body text NOT retrieved.

citations.title: Residents' Files
citations.requirement: The administrator or on-site manager keeps an individual file for each resident. Confidential; disclosed only to the resident, representative or legal surrogate, DCH agents and those with written authorization. Available for inspection and copying by the resident or representative and by DCH. Contents include: identifying information; physician, hospital and pharmacy of choice; record of monetary transactions with itemized receipts; record and receipt of valuables held in safekeeping; health information (appraisals, diagnoses, diets, medications, orders); inventory of personal valuables; signed Resident's Rights form; signed admission agreement; powers of attorney; living will, DPOA-HC or Georgia advance directive (forms available at admission); signed end-of-life medical orders.

citations.title: Supporting Residents Rights and Obtaining Feedback
citations.requirement: Rights cannot be waived except by the resident, representative or legal surrogate as the rules allow. Care must be adequate and appropriate. No punishment or harassment for enforcing rights. Rights to vote, choose activities and schedules, interact with the community, and privacy in the room (staff knock first). Free and private communication without staff censorship. Married residents may share a room, and no more than two residents may share a bedroom. Freedom from coercion to assign money, valuables or property to the community. (u) A resident without a court commitment or authorized representative may self-discharge on 30 days written notice. (v) Access to the State Long-Term Care Ombudsman Program (O.C.G.A. 31-8-50 et seq.), with the assigned ombudsman's name, address and phone posted in a common area. Paragraphs on feedback were not retrieved.

citations.title: Procedures for Change in Resident's Condition
citations.requirement: Full text read. On an accident or sudden adverse change the community acts immediately, notifies the representative or legal surrogate, and records the change and response in the resident file. For an unresponsive resident: hospice enrollee, call the hospice, then the health care agent, then EMS and CPR if no DNR. Valid DNR: honor it in good faith. Health care agent under O.C.G.A. 31-32-1 et seq.: call the agent, and if unavailable with no DNR call EMS and start CPR. No hospice, DNR or directive: call EMS and start CPR unless clearly futile and no physician, authorized RN or PA is on site. Staff need ready access to emergency numbers and resident information, including during transport. The administrator or on-site manager must start an immediate investigation of the cause of an accident, injury or death, report to the representative or legal surrogate, and keep copies in the resident file and a central quality-assurance file.

citations.title: Death of a Resident
citations.requirement: Rule number and title confirmed from the official index. Body text NOT retrieved; read before finalizing procedures.

citations.title: Immediate Transfers of Residents
citations.requirement: Rule number and title confirmed from the official index. Body text NOT retrieved.

citations.title: Discharge or Transfer of Residents
citations.requirement: (1) Each admission agreement includes a written procedure for discharge and transfer. The administrator or on-site manager contacts the representative or legal surrogate when discharge or transfer is needed. The community gives 30 days written notice of intent to discharge or transfer unless an immediate transfer is required. Later paragraphs not retrieved.

citations.title: Reports to the Department
citations.requirement: Full text read. Call local police within 30 minutes of actual knowledge that a resident is missing (Mattie's Call Act). Report the start and end of a Mattie's Call to DCH within 30 minutes of the contact with law enforcement. Report serious incidents to DCH within 24 hours of the incident or of reasonable cause to believe one occurred: accidental or unanticipated death not tied to the natural course of illness; serious injury needing medical attention; rape, assault, battery, abuse, neglect or exploitation (Long-Term Care Resident Abuse Reporting Act); external disaster or emergency affecting safe operation; an owner, director or employee acquiring a criminal record. Report contents: community and administrator names, incident date and discovery date, incident type and brief description, immediate corrective or preventive action. DCH may open a separate complaint investigation.

citations.title: Deemed Status
citations.requirement: Rule number and title confirmed from the official index. Body text NOT retrieved.

citations.title: Variances and Waivers
citations.requirement: Rule number and title confirmed from the official index. Body text NOT retrieved.

citations.title: Enforcement of Licensing Requirements
citations.requirement: Rule number and title confirmed from the official index. Body text NOT retrieved.

citations.title: Application for Permit (PCH)
citations.requirement: PCH application on DCH format with truthful disclosure. Sketch or drawing of the home and grounds showing windows, doors, room measurements and bed placement, plus ownership or lease documentation. Administrator or on-site manager name before the permit issues. Disclosure of owners with 10% or more and the registered agent. Local zoning addressed. A CPA financial stability affidavit is required for an initial application of 25 or more beds. No PCH may operate and no resident may be admitted without a current permit. No memory care center may operate without a current certificate.

citations.title: Permits (PCH)
citations.requirement: Valid permit before operating. Permit displayed conspicuously. May not exceed approved licensed capacity. Permit invalid and returned when the home ceases to operate, moves, or ownership changes (text truncated after this point in the retrieved copy).

citations.title: Governing Body (PCH)
citations.requirement: The governing body oversees compliance with Title 31 Ch. 7, and DCH Ch. 111-8-25, 111-8-62 and 111-8-100. It keeps DCH supplied with current contact information (name, email for notices, physical addresses, phones for the governing body and administrator or on-site manager) and makes staff accountable for delivering notices to it. Required policies cover services, admissions/discharges/immediate transfers, refunds, staff training and evaluation, house rules, rights, and medication management (list continues; truncated in retrieved text).

citations.title: PCH Administrator Qualifications
citations.requirement: Per fact-checked research: for fewer than 25 beds, an associate's degree, or a GED/high school diploma plus 2 years' licensed PCH or healthcare experience, and age 21+. For 25+ beds, a valid Board of Long-Term Care Facility Administrators license within 60 days of hire.

citations.title: PCH Workforce Qualifications and Training
citations.requirement: Per fact-checked research: on-site managers and responsible staff persons 21+; under-18 staff only under line-of-sight supervision; new staff work-related training including emergency first aid and CPR certification within 60 days.

citations.title: Definitions (PCH)
citations.requirement: Legal surrogate definition: no member of the governing body, administration or staff, or their family members, may serve as a resident's legal surrogate. A copy of any power of attorney must be kept in the resident file. Also defines abuse, exploitation, physical and chemical restraint, memory care center, representative, and similar terms.

citations.title: Operation of memory care center; certificate required; staffing and training requirements
citations.requirement: Memory care centers: all staff get at least 4 hours of dementia-specific orientation within the first 30 days. Direct care staff complete at least 16 hours of dementia training within the first 30 days of working independently with dementia residents, then at least 8 hours annually. Keep documentation of course content, instructor qualifications, agendas and attendance rosters.

citations.cite: O.C.G.A. § 31-8-80 et seq. (Long-Term Care Facility Resident Abuse Reporting Act)
citations.title: Resident Abuse Reporting Act (as cited in Rule 111-8-63-.30 and .09(2)(a))
citations.requirement: Cited by Rule .30(2)(c) as the reporting standard. Rule .09(2)(a) cites O.C.G.A. § 31-8-81 et seq. and requires each employee to receive a copy during initial training. Statute text was not retrieved.

citations.cite: O.C.G.A. § 31-8-50 et seq. (State Long-Term Care Ombudsman Program)
citations.title: Ombudsman Program (as cited in Rule 111-8-63-.25(v))
citations.requirement: Rule .25(v) gives residents access to the ombudsman program and requires posting the assigned ombudsman's name, address and phone. Statute text was not retrieved.

citations.cite: O.C.G.A. § 31-32-1 et seq. (Georgia advance directive for health care)
citations.title: Advance directives (as cited in Rule 111-8-63-.26)
citations.requirement: Rule .26(2)(c) cites it for the health care agent's authority. Statute text was not retrieved.

citations.title: Mattie's Call Act (as cited in Rule 111-8-63-.30(1))
citations.requirement: Cited by Rule .30(1) for the 30-minute police notification of a missing resident. Statute text was not retrieved.

citations.title: Rules and Regulations for Criminal Background Checks (as incorporated by Rule 111-8-63-.09(11)-(13))
citations.requirement: Owners, administrators, on-site managers and direct access employees need a satisfactory fingerprint records check determination before serving. Chapter text was not retrieved; definitions and timing come from Ch. 111-8-12 and the DCH GCHEXS process.

citations.title: Rules and Regulations for Disaster Preparedness Plans (as incorporated by Rule 111-8-63-.14(1))
citations.requirement: The ALC must comply with Ch. 111-8-16. Chapter text was not retrieved.

citations.title: Rules and Regulations for General Licensing and Enforcement Requirements (as cited in Rules 111-8-63-.05(3) and .07(1))
citations.requirement: Source of licensing fees, application completeness and enforcement. Chapter text was not retrieved.

citations.title: Rules and Regulations for Proxy Caregivers Used in Licensed Healthcare Facilities (as cited in Rules 111-8-63-.03(kk), .09(8), .09(16))
citations.requirement: Proxy caregivers need training under Ch. 111-8-100, and only CMAs may administer medications for the community (Rule .09(8)). Chapter text was not retrieved.

citations.cite: DCH Schedule of Licensure Activity Fees
citations.title: Application, license, memory care, late and replacement fees
citations.requirement: Per fact-checked research: $300 non-refundable application fee; annual license $350 (PCH 2-24 beds), $750 (ALC 25-50), $1,500 (ALC 51+); memory care certificate $200 per year; $150 late fee when 60 days past due; $50 permit replacement.

citations.title: ALC application documents, inspections, GCHEXS checks, GAHLES portal (updated 07/13/26)
citations.requirement: Per fact-checked research: DCH Office of Health Planning Letter of Determination; State Fire Marshal report with no violations and capacity load (within 12 months); electrician compliance form (within 6 months); private water test within 6 months if no city or county water; GCHEXS fingerprint checks for administrators and owners with 10%+ (letter within 12 months); communities are inspected without notice and policies must be available for review; Affidavit of Compliance.

citations.title: Electronic visit verification for Medicaid personal care services, implemented by DCH
citations.requirement: Per fact-checked research: Georgia uses Netsmart Mobile Caregiver+. Personal support services under CCSP and SOURCE are listed under HCPCS T1019. Applicable claims with dates of service on or after Sept 14, 2026 must go through EVV. Whether EVV applies to the ALS placement service itself is unverified; confirm with DCH.

citations.title: Georgia Elderly and Disabled Waiver (expires 11/08/2027)
citations.requirement: Per fact-checked research: authority for CCSP and SOURCE, including Alternative Living Services in licensed personal care homes. Waivers do not pay room and board.

citations.cite: Board of Long-Term Care Facility Administrators - Application for Initial Licensure as ALC or PCH Administrator (form dated 11.2022)
citations.title: Administrator initial licensure application
citations.requirement: Per fact-checked research: $100 application fee plus $10 (paper) or $5 (online) processing fee. At least 1 year of full-time experience (1,560 hours in the preceding 12 months) plus a board-approved administration program. The license is biennial and expires Dec 31 of odd-numbered years. The Board's phone is 404-424-9966. Confirm the current fee.

citations.cite: Rule 111-8-62 (staffing and change of ownership provisions)
citations.title: PCH staffing ratios and 30-day change-of-ownership notice
citations.requirement: Per fact-checked research: at least 30 days written notice to DCH and residents of a change of ownership (60 days for impending bankruptcy or eviction). The PCH staff ratio of 1 awake direct care staff per 15 residents in waking hours and per 25 in non-waking hours comes from third-party-hosted text and is NOT confirmed against current official text; verify before use.

citations.title: Legal authority for Ch. 111-8-63 (Rule 111-8-63-.01)
citations.requirement: Statutory authority for the ALC rules; Rule .09 notes also cite O.C.G.A. 31-2-8, 31-2-9, 31-7-1 et seq. and 43-26-12.

policies.category: ALC: Rule 111-8-63-.07(2), policies and procedures (a) through (p)
policies.title: Services Available in the Community (Personal Services, Assisted Living Care, Memory Care, Proxy Caregivers)
state_specifics: Community provides assisted living care, including protective care and watchful oversight (111-8-63-.17(1)).
Services and marketing must match the license, the licensed residential care profile and the rules. Only a licensed ALC may hold itself out as offering assisted living care (.10).

Periodic or short-term medical and nursing services are not community services; the resident purchases them. Care planning, training, medication administration and competency checks are excepted (.17(11)).
No memory care center may operate without a current DCH certificate, and the profile must carry the written memory care description (.19).
List any designated proxy caregiver services (Ch. 111-8-100) here. Describe only services the permit allows.

policies.category: ALC: Rule 111-8-63-.07(2), policies and procedures (a) through (p)
policies.title: Staffing Plan and Ratios That Rise With Assisted Self-Preservation Needs
state_specifics: At least 2 trained direct care staff on site 24 hours a day whenever residents are present, with at least 1 on each occupied floor (111-8-63-.09(4), (18)).

Monthly average ratios for minimal-need residents: 1 awake direct care staff per 15 residents in waking hours and 1 per 20 in non-waking hours. Ratios increase as the number of assisted-self-preservation residents increases.
RN or LPN on site 8 hrs/week (1-30 residents), 16 (31-60), 24 (61-90), 40 (more than 90) (.09(18)).
Staffing plans and schedules are kept 1 year (.09(21)). A new hire still inside the 60-day training window does not count toward the 2 fully trained staff.
The plan must also cover relief staff and absences of regularly scheduled staff.

policies.category: ALC: Rule 111-8-63-.07(2), policies and procedures (a) through (p)
policies.title: Admissions, Discharges, Immediate Transfers and Refunds
state_specifics: Admission profile (.15(1)): age 18+; no active TB; no need for continuous medical or nursing care; no need for physical or chemical restraints, isolation or confinement; able to take part in transfers and in social and leisure activities.
Do not admit or retain a resident who needs more care than the community is authorized or able to provide (.07(2)(c)).
Give 30 days' written notice of discharge or transfer unless an immediate transfer is required (.29(1)). The administrator contacts the representative or legal surrogate.
The admission agreement states the refund policy on death, transfer or discharge (.16). Write the refund calculation method and timeline into this policy.
Immediate-transfer triggers and steps follow .28; the body text of .28 was not retrieved, so confirm it before finalizing.

policies.category: ALC: Rule 111-8-63-.07(2), policies and procedures (a) through (p)
policies.title: Staff Training and Ongoing Evaluation (Including Memory Care and Proxy Caregiver Training)
state_specifics: All staff are trained within 60 days of hire. Hands-on staff also complete first aid and CPR with return demonstration within 60 days (.09(2)-(3)).
Hands-on staff, including the administrator, complete 24 CE hours in year one and 16 hours per year after (.09(5)-(6)).
Each employee receives a copy of the Long-Term Care Facility Resident Abuse Reporting Act during initial training (.09(2)(a)). Keep training records (.09(7)).

Memory care (O.C.G.A. 31-7-12.4): 4 hrs dementia orientation for all staff within 30 days. Direct care staff need 16 hrs of dementia training within 30 days of working independently, then 8 hrs per year.
Proxy caregivers are trained under Ch. 111-8-100. Add a written annual performance evaluation for every employee.

policies.category: ALC: Rule 111-8-63-.07(2), policies and procedures (a) through (p)
policies.title: House Rules and Their Enforcement
state_specifics: House rules are written, given to residents and representatives, and applied without punishment or harassment of anyone enforcing rights (.25).
Rules may not restrict free access to common areas or lock a resident into or out of the bedroom (.17(7)).
No more than 2 residents may share a bedroom; married residents may share a room (.25).
Set rules for smoking, visitors, pets and alcohol here so they do not conflict with resident rights or fire safety.
The community must not allow other businesses to intrude on residents' quiet enjoyment (.06).

policies.category: ALC: Rule 111-8-63-.07(2), policies and procedures (a) through (p)
policies.title: Protecting Resident Rights
federal: 42 CFR 441.301(c) (HCBS settings, if Medicaid waiver residents are served)
state_specifics: Rights may be waived only by the resident, representative or legal surrogate as the rules allow. Care must be adequate and appropriate (.25).
Rights to vote, choose activities and schedules, and have private communication without staff censorship. Staff knock before entering a room.
No coercion to assign money, valuables or property to the community.
Signed Resident's Rights form kept in the resident file (.24).
Residents may self-discharge on 30 days' written notice if there is no court commitment or authorized representative (.25(u)).

policies.category: ALC: Rule 111-8-63-.07(2), policies and procedures (a) through (p)
policies.title: Medication Management, Procurement, Certified Medication Aides and Professional Oversight
state_specifics: Only certified medication aides (CMAs) administer medications. Check the Georgia CMA Registry and run skills competency checks (111-8-63-.20).
An RN or pharmacist does quarterly random observations and a pharmacist does quarterly drug regimen reviews. An RN, pharmacist or physician does annual competency reviews.
Orders are required for all medications, including OTC. New prescriptions and the MAR are updated within 48 hours, and a MAR is kept daily.

Store medications under lock and key in original containers. Controlled substances go in a locked cabinet or box of substantial construction with a daily-updated log, and duplicate keys stay on site. Dispose per FDA/EPA guidance.

Residents able to self-administer may keep medications securely. Staff assistance is limited to the listed tasks, and EpiPen use needs a written protocol and a 911 call. Liquid morphine is limited to 50 ml per hospice resident.

policies.category: ALC: Rule 111-8-63-.07(2), policies and procedures (a) through (p)
policies.title: Health and Hygiene: Infection Control, Work and Return-to-Work, Foodborne Illness, Reportable Diseases
state_specifics: TB screening and physical exam within 12 months before any employee provides care (111-8-63-.09(10)). No admission of a resident with active TB (.15(1)).
Rule .23 (infection control, sanitation, supplies) body text was not retrieved. Confirm its requirements before finalizing.
Write exclusion and return-to-work criteria for ill staff (vomiting, diarrhea, fever, respiratory illness, skin infections).
Foodborne illness controls: perishables at or below 41 degrees F (.21).
Reportable diseases are reported to the local health district per Georgia Department of Public Health requirements.

policies.category: ALC: Rule 111-8-63-.07(2), policies and procedures (a) through (p)
policies.title: Investigation and Reporting of Abuse, Neglect, Exploitation, Wandering, Accidents, Injuries and Changes in Condition
state_specifics: Report to DCH within 24 hours of an incident or of reasonable cause to believe one occurred: unanticipated or accidental death, serious injury needing medical attention, rape, assault, battery, abuse, neglect or exploitation, external disaster, or an owner, director or employee acquiring a criminal record (111-8-63-.30).
Wandering or missing resident: call police within 30 minutes of actual knowledge and report the start and end of the Mattie's Call to DCH within 30 minutes of law enforcement contact (.30(1)).
The administrator or on-site manager starts an immediate investigation of the cause of an accident, injury or death. Report to the representative or legal surrogate (.26).
Keep copies in the resident file and in a central quality-assurance file (.26).
Report contents: community and administrator names, incident and discovery dates, incident type and brief description, and immediate corrective or preventive action.

policies.category: ALC: Rule 111-8-63-.07(2), policies and procedures (a) through (p)
policies.title: Staff Discipline for Conduct Inconsistent With Community Policies
state_specifics: Staff may not be impaired on duty (111-8-63-.09(17)). Write the discipline steps for suspected impairment.
Staff may not coerce residents to assign money, valuables or property (.25).
Remove staff from resident contact pending investigation of any abuse, neglect or exploitation allegation.
An employee acquiring a criminal record is reported to DCH within 24 hours (.30).
Document progressive discipline and keep it in the personnel file (kept 3 years after departure, .09).

policies.category: ALC: Rule 111-8-63-.07(2), policies and procedures (a) through (p)
policies.title: Emergency Preparedness, Drills and Evacuation
state_specifics: Comply with Ch. 111-8-16 (Disaster Preparedness Plans) (111-8-63-.14(1)). The plan is accessible to staff, residents and families.
The plan names the staff positions responsible for implementing it and for obtaining emergency medical attention.
Post evacuation maps with marked escape routes on each floor. Keep a clear emergency route through common areas.
If an emergency forces relocation, give timely notice of the new address to residents, family contacts, representatives and DCH.
The State Fire Marshal report must show no violations and state the capacity load. Fire drill frequency and records follow Rule .13 and Fire Marshal requirements; confirm against current text.

policies.category: ALC: Rule 111-8-63-.07(2), policies and procedures (a) through (p)
policies.title: Quality Assurance Review and Resident/Family Feedback
state_specifics: Keep the central quality-assurance file with investigations of accidents, injuries and deaths (111-8-63-.26).
Review incident trends, inspection findings and plans of correction on a set schedule.
Obtain resident and family feedback (surveys, council meetings) and record the action taken.
Inspection report disputes and plans of correction are due within 10 days of receipt (.10).
Keep the licensed residential care profile accurate.

policies.category: ALC: Rule 111-8-63-.07(2), policies and procedures (a) through (p)
policies.title: Use of Volunteers and Proxy Caregivers
state_specifics: Volunteers receive orientation on resident rights and basic safety precautions before contact with residents.
Volunteers are not counted toward staffing minimums and do not perform hands-on care or medication tasks.
State whether proxy caregivers are permitted. If so, set the oversight required under Ch. 111-8-100 and the Rule .17(8) options.
Proxy caregivers are trained under Ch. 111-8-100. Only CMAs may administer medications for the community (.09(8)).
Define proxy caregiver per Rule .03 and keep a roster of designated proxies.

policies.category: ALC: Rule 111-8-63-.07(2), policies and procedures (a) through (p)
policies.title: Safety and Security Precautions Against Harm by Other Residents, Proxy Caregivers and Outside Individuals
state_specifics: Before admission, the administrator or on-site manager documents a National Sex Offender Registry inquiry or fingerprint check (111-8-63-.15(2)).
Document added safety measures for registered sex offenders or violent offenders.
Visitor, vendor and contractor sign-in, and screening for outside individuals who routinely come into the community (hospice, home health, proxy caregivers).
Staff wear ID badges (.09(22)). Residents keep private communication and room privacy (.25).
Use a resident-to-resident incident protocol: separate, assess, notify, report and revise the care plan.

policies.category: PCH: Rule 111-8-62-.07(3), policies and procedures (a) through (p)
policies.title: Services Available in the Home (Personal Services, Memory Care, Proxy Caregivers)
state_specifics: A PCH may not provide assisted living care unless it holds an ALC license (Ch. 111-8-62).
No memory care center may operate without a current DCH certificate (111-8-62-.05); fee $200 per year.
List personal services, meals, laundry and supervision actually provided, and any designated proxy caregiver services (Ch. 111-8-100).
Services and marketing must match the PCH permit.
Check this text against current Ch. 111-8-62 before finalizing. The ALC rule 111-8-63-.17 is a close analog.

policies.category: PCH: Rule 111-8-62-.07(3), policies and procedures (a) through (p)
policies.title: Admissions, Discharges, Immediate Transfers and Refunds
state_specifics: Do not admit or retain residents who need more care than the home is authorized or able to provide (.07(3)(b)).
Refunds on transfer or discharge are written into this policy and the admission agreement (.07(3)(c)).
The ALC rule gives 30 days' written notice of discharge or transfer unless an immediate transfer is required (111-8-63-.29); confirm the PCH rule matches.
The ALC admission profile (age 18+, no active TB, no continuous nursing need, no restraint need) is a model; confirm the PCH criteria.
Change-of-ownership or closure: at least 30 days' written notice to DCH and residents (60 days for impending bankruptcy or eviction).

policies.category: PCH: Rule 111-8-62-.07(3), policies and procedures (a) through (p)
policies.title: Staff Training and Ongoing Evaluation (Including Memory Care and Proxy Caregivers)
state_specifics: New staff complete work-related training, including emergency first aid and CPR certification, within the first 60 days (111-8-62-.09).
On-site managers and responsible staff are 21+. Anyone under 18 works only under direct line-of-sight supervision.
Memory care (O.C.G.A. 31-7-12.4): 4 hrs dementia orientation for all staff within 30 days. Direct care staff need 16 hrs within 30 days of independent work, then 8 hrs per year.
Proxy caregivers need training under Ch. 111-8-100.
Keep training records and an annual written staff evaluation.

policies.category: PCH: Rule 111-8-62-.07(3), policies and procedures (a) through (p)
policies.title: House Rules and Their Enforcement
state_specifics: House rules are written, given to residents at admission and enforced without retaliation.
Cover smoking, visitors, pets and alcohol. Rules may not override resident rights.
The ALC rule bars locking residents in or out of bedrooms and restricting common areas (111-8-63-.17(7)); apply the same standard and confirm in 111-8-62.
No more than 2 residents per bedroom in the ALC rule; confirm the PCH rule.
Residents sign an acknowledgment of the house rules.

policies.category: PCH: Rule 111-8-62-.07(3), policies and procedures (a) through (p)
policies.title: Protecting Resident Rights
federal: 42 CFR 441.301(c) (HCBS settings, if Medicaid waiver residents are served)
state_specifics: The governing body must adopt rights policies (111-8-62-.07).
No member of the governing body, administration or staff, or their family, may serve as a resident's legal surrogate (111-8-62-.03).
Post the assigned ombudsman's name, address and phone in a common area (ALC analog 111-8-63-.25(v)).
No punishment or harassment for enforcing rights. Free, private communication.
Keep the signed Resident's Rights form in the resident file.

policies.category: PCH: Rule 111-8-62-.07(3), policies and procedures (a) through (p)
policies.title: Medication Management, Procurement and Professional Oversight
state_specifics: The governing body must adopt medication management policies (111-8-62-.07).
Follow the ALC standard (111-8-63-.20) where the PCH rule mirrors it, and confirm each paragraph in Ch. 111-8-62: orders for all medications including OTC; locked storage; daily MAR.
Controlled substances in a locked box with a daily-updated log. Disposal per FDA/EPA guidance.
Name who may assist or administer medications and the professional (RN or pharmacist) overseeing them.
Residents able to self-administer do so with secure storage.

policies.category: PCH: Rule 111-8-62-.07(3), policies and procedures (a) through (p)
policies.title: Health and Hygiene: Infection Control, Work and Return-to-Work, Foodborne Illness, Reportable Diseases
state_specifics: TB screening and physical for employees within 12 months before providing care (ALC analog 111-8-63-.09(10)); confirm the PCH paragraph.
Write staff exclusion and return-to-work criteria for infectious illness.
Foodborne illness response: keep perishables at or below 41 degrees F (ALC .21 analog), and isolate and report outbreaks.
Reportable diseases go to the local health district per Georgia Department of Public Health requirements.
Hand hygiene, standard precautions, sharps, laundry and housekeeping procedures.

policies.category: PCH: Rule 111-8-62-.07(3), policies and procedures (a) through (p)
policies.title: Investigation and Reporting of Abuse, Neglect, Exploitation, Wandering, Accidents, Injuries and Changes in Condition
state_specifics: Use the ALC reporting standard as the model and confirm the PCH paragraphs: serious incidents to DCH within 24 hours (111-8-63-.30).
Missing resident: call police within 30 minutes and report the start and end of the Mattie's Call to DCH within 30 minutes.
Start an immediate investigation of the cause of any accident, injury or death. Notify the representative or legal surrogate.
Keep copies in the resident file and a central QA file.
Report abuse, neglect and exploitation under the Long-Term Care Facility Resident Abuse Reporting Act.

policies.category: PCH: Rule 111-8-62-.07(3), policies and procedures (a) through (p)
policies.title: Staff Discipline for Conduct Inconsistent With Home Policies
state_specifics: Write progressive discipline steps and document them in the personnel file.
No impairment on duty (ALC analog 111-8-63-.09(17)).
Immediate removal from resident contact pending investigation of abuse, neglect or exploitation.
Staff may not coerce residents to assign money or property.
An employee, owner or director acquiring a criminal record is reported to DCH within 24 hours (ALC analog .30).

policies.category: PCH: Rule 111-8-62-.07(3), policies and procedures (a) through (p)
policies.title: Emergency Preparedness, Drills and Evacuation
state_specifics: Written disaster plan under Ch. 111-8-16, accessible to staff, residents and families. It names the responsible staff positions.
Post evacuation maps showing escape routes on each floor.
Document fire and evacuation drills per Fire Marshal and DCH requirements; confirm the frequency in current Ch. 111-8-62.
Notify residents, families, representatives and DCH of the relocation address if an emergency forces relocation.
Keep an emergency contact list and resident information for transport.

policies.category: PCH: Rule 111-8-62-.07(3), policies and procedures (a) through (p)
policies.title: Quality Assurance and Peer Review Using Serious Incident Reports and Feedback
state_specifics: Review serious-incident reports and investigations on a set schedule and record corrective action.
Collect resident and family feedback and use it to improve care.
Keep the central quality-assurance file (ALC analog 111-8-63-.26).
Use peer review of care practices (medication errors, falls, discharges) and document findings.
Review inspection results and plans of correction.

policies.category: PCH: Rule 111-8-62-.07(3), policies and procedures (a) through (p)
policies.title: Volunteers With Unsupervised Access and Proxy Caregivers
state_specifics: Volunteers with unsupervised access to residents receive orientation on resident rights and basic safety precautions.
Volunteers do not count toward staffing or perform medication tasks.
State whether proxy caregivers are used and set the oversight required under Ch. 111-8-100.
Keep a roster of volunteers and designated proxy caregivers.
Check the background-check requirement for volunteers with unsupervised access against Ch. 111-8-12.

policies.category: PCH: Rule 111-8-62-.07(3), policies and procedures (a) through (p)
policies.title: Safety and Security Precautions Against Harm by Other Residents, Proxy Caregivers and Outside Individuals
state_specifics: Before admission, document a National Sex Offender Registry inquiry or fingerprint check (ALC analog 111-8-63-.15(2)); confirm the PCH paragraph.
Document added safety measures for registered sex offenders or violent offenders.
Visitor and vendor sign-in. Screen outside individuals who routinely come into the home, such as hospice and home health staff.
Staff wear ID badges (ALC analog .09(22)).
Resident-to-resident incident protocol: separate, assess, notify, report and revise the care plan.

policies.category: PCH: Rule 111-8-62-.07(3), policies and procedures (a) through (p)
policies.title: Staffing Plan Based on Resident Needs and Coverage for Absences
state_specifics: Planning ratio from third-party-hosted rule text: 1 awake direct care staff per 15 residents in waking hours and per 25 in non-waking hours. Verify against current Ch. 111-8-62 with DCH before finalizing.
The plan reflects the specific needs of residents and names backup and on-call staff for absences of regularly scheduled staff.
An owner-administrator who is off duty cannot be counted as the awake overnight staff.
Managers and responsible staff are 21+. Hands-on staff are 18+ (under 18 only with line-of-sight supervision).
Keep schedules and the staffing plan on file for inspection.

policies.category: Governance, Licensure and Inspections
policies.title: Licensure, Permit Posting, Licensed Capacity, Inspections and Change of Ownership
state_specifics: A valid DCH permit is required before admitting any resident. Display it conspicuously. It is not transferable and is invalid on a move or ownership change. Never exceed the licensed capacity on the permit (111-8-63-.06; 111-8-62-.06).

Disclose the ALC classification in marketing. Fees: $300 application (non-refundable); annual license $350 (PCH 2-24 beds), $750 (ALC 25-50), $1,500 (ALC 51+); $200 memory care; $150 late fee at 60 days past due; $50 permit replacement.
Inspections are unannounced. Policies must be available for review (DCH checklist). Disputes and written plans of correction are due within 10 days of receipt (111-8-63-.10).
Display the most recent inspection report and plan of correction. If the community has a website, link the previous 18 months of reports (.10).
Change of ownership: at least 30 days' written notice to DCH and residents (60 days for impending bankruptcy or eviction); the new owner needs a new permit.

policies.category: Governance, Licensure and Inspections
policies.title: Governing Body, Administrator Qualifications, DCH Contact Information and Document Control
state_specifics: The governing body oversees compliance with Ch. 111-8-62 or 111-8-63, 111-8-25 and 111-8-100. It keeps DCH supplied with current names, emails and phones. PCH program contact: pchprogram.hfrd@dch.ga.gov.
PCH under 25 beds: administrator needs an associate's degree, or a GED/high school diploma plus 2 years of PCH or healthcare experience, and must be 21+ (111-8-62-.08).
25+ beds (ALC or PCH): a Board of Long-Term Care Facility Administrators license within 60 days of hire. Board phone 404-424-9966. Biennial license expires Dec 31 of odd-numbered years.
Initial 25+ bed applications need a CPA financial stability affidavit (going concern 2 years) and disclosure of owners with 10%+ and the registered agent.
Review the manual at least annually. Keep a revision log and a dated approval signature from the governing body.

policies.category: Resident Rights
policies.title: Grievances, Complaints and Ombudsman Access
state_specifics: The admission agreement describes the complaint process (111-8-63-.16).
Post the assigned ombudsman's name, address and phone in a common area. Residents have access to the State Long-Term Care Ombudsman Program (.25(v)).
No punishment or harassment of any resident or staff who raises a complaint or enforces rights.
Log each grievance, the investigation, the response date and the resolution.
Tell residents they may complain to DCH.

policies.category: Resident Rights
policies.title: Admission Agreement, Fees, Rate Increases and Deposits
state_specifics: Plain-language agreement consistent with the licensed residential care profile. It states all fees and what they cover (111-8-63-.16).
Written notice at least 30 days before any personal-service charge increase and at least 60 days before any room-and-board increase.

The agreement includes continuous assessment and referral or transfer on change of condition, a complaint process, transportation terms with emergency transport available at all times, and a refund policy on death, transfer or discharge.
Have a Georgia attorney review the agreement.
Obtain signatures from the resident or representative and place the agreement in the resident file.

policies.category: Resident Rights
policies.title: Resident Funds, Valuables and Personal Property
state_specifics: Keep a record of monetary transactions with itemized receipts (111-8-63-.24).
Give a receipt for valuables held in safekeeping. Keep an inventory of personal valuables in the file.
No coercion to assign money, valuables or property to the community (.25).
Keep resident funds separate from operating funds.
Quarterly reconciliation signed by the administrator.

policies.category: Resident Rights
policies.title: Advance Directives, Legal Surrogates and Powers of Attorney
state_specifics: Keep a living will, DPOA-HC or Georgia advance directive, and signed end-of-life medical orders, in the file. Make forms available at admission (111-8-63-.24).
Valid DNR: honor it in good faith. Health care agent: call the agent. Otherwise call EMS and start CPR (.26).
No member of the governing body, administration or staff, or their family, may be a resident's legal surrogate (111-8-62-.03).
Keep a copy of any power of attorney in the resident file.
Train staff to find the code status quickly.

policies.category: Resident Rights
policies.title: Privacy, Confidentiality and HIPAA
state_specifics: Resident files are confidential and disclosed only to the resident, representative or legal surrogate, DCH agents and those with written authorization (111-8-63-.24).
Residents and representatives may inspect and copy the file.
Staff knock before entering resident rooms. Private communication is protected (.25).
If the community is a HIPAA covered entity (for example, bills Medicaid electronically), designate a privacy officer, issue a notice of privacy practices and sign business associate agreements.
Photographs, social media and marketing use require written consent.

policies.category: Resident Rights
policies.title: Nondiscrimination, Disability Access and Language Access
state_specifics: Admission is based on the admission profile and the community's ability to meet needs, not race, national origin, religion, sex or disability.
Provide interpreters and translated key documents for limited-English-proficient residents. The admission agreement is in plain language (111-8-63-.16).
Reasonable accommodations and service-animal handling under ADA.
Residents may choose activities and schedules (.25).
Post a nondiscrimination notice.

policies.category: Admission, Retention and Discharge
policies.title: Pre-Admission Screening, Admission Criteria and Retention Limits
state_specifics: Applicant must be 18+, free of active TB, not need continuous medical or nursing care, not need restraints, isolation or confinement for behavior, and be able to participate in transfers and in social and leisure activities (111-8-63-.15(1)).
The administrator or on-site manager documents the evaluation, including a National Sex Offender Registry inquiry or fingerprint check and added safety measures where needed (.15(2)).
A physician examination on DCH forms is part of the admission packet (.15).
Admission and retention decisions must not exceed what the community is authorized or able to provide (.07(2)(c)).
Do not exceed the licensed capacity.

policies.category: Admission, Retention and Discharge
policies.title: Resident Assessment, Reassessment and Care Plan
state_specifics: Needs assessment covers family supports, ADL function, physical care, medical information, cognitive and behavioral impairments and preferences (111-8-63-.17(2)).
Written care plan within 14 days of admission, updated at least annually, when needs change substantially, and on assignment to a memory care center (.17(3)).
Memory care centers reassess at triggers before the customary quarterly review (.19).
Assistive devices need a physician/NP/PA order, a written care plan and resident consent (.03).
The resident or representative takes part in and signs the plan.

policies.category: Admission, Retention and Discharge
policies.title: Discharge, Transfer and Relocation Notice
state_specifics: Give 30 days' written notice of intent to discharge or transfer unless an immediate transfer is required (111-8-63-.29(1)).
The administrator or on-site manager contacts the representative or legal surrogate when discharge or transfer is needed.
A resident without a court commitment or authorized representative may self-discharge on 30 days' written notice (.25(u)).
Provide a written discharge procedure in every admission agreement.
Refund or settlement per the admission agreement. Include the transfer of medications, records and personal property.

policies.category: Health and Care Services
policies.title: Change of Condition, Physician Notification and Hospital Transfer
state_specifics: On an accident or sudden adverse change, act immediately, notify the representative or legal surrogate, and record the change and response in the file (111-8-63-.26).

Unresponsive resident: hospice enrollee, call hospice first. Valid DNR, honor it. Health care agent, call the agent. Otherwise call EMS and start CPR unless clearly futile and no physician, RN or PA is on site.
Staff have ready access to emergency numbers and resident information, including during transport.
Serious injury requiring medical attention is reported to DCH within 24 hours (.30).
The agreement provides for continuous assessment and referral or transfer on change of condition.

policies.category: Health and Care Services
policies.title: Dementia and Memory Care (Certified Memory Care Centers)
state_specifics: No memory care center operates without a current DCH certificate; $200 per year. The ALC packet requires a current ALC permit first.

The profile carries the written 12-element description (philosophy, staffing, admission criteria, reassessment, environment and security, activities, fees, discharge, emergencies, family involvement) (111-8-63-.19).

Staffing: 1 dementia-trained direct care staff per 12 residents in waking hours and per 15 in non-waking hours (monthly average). RN/LPN hours: 8/wk (1-12 residents), 16 (13-30), 24 (31-40), 40 (more than 40).
Training (O.C.G.A. 31-7-12.4): 4 hrs orientation within 30 days. Direct care staff need 16 hrs within 30 days, then 8 hrs per year. Keep agendas, instructor qualifications and rosters.
No chemical or physical restraints for behavior control.

policies.category: Health and Care Services
policies.title: Falls Prevention and Skin Integrity
state_specifics: Injury includes pressure ulcers not properly cared for (111-8-63-.03). Treat them as reportable.
Fall risk screening at admission and after any fall or condition change. Update the care plan (.17(3)).
Serious fall injury requiring medical attention is reported to DCH within 24 hours and investigated immediately (.26, .30).
Assistive devices need an order, a care plan and consent (.03).
Limited nursing services (care completed within 7 days or intermittently) are provided only as the rules allow.

policies.category: Health and Care Services
policies.title: Hospice, Home Health, Nursing Services and Death of a Resident
state_specifics: Periodic or short-term nursing and medical services are purchased by the resident, not provided as community services (111-8-63-.17(11)).
Hospice enrollee: call hospice first when the resident is unresponsive (.26). Liquid morphine limited to 50 ml per hospice resident (.20).
An accidental or unanticipated death not tied to the natural course of illness is reported to DCH within 24 hours and investigated immediately (.26, .30).
Refund on death is handled per the admission agreement (.16).
Rule .27 (Death of a Resident) body text was not retrieved. Confirm notice and release procedures before finalizing.

policies.category: Safety and Protection
policies.title: Elopement, Missing Resident and Mattie's Call
state_specifics: Call local police within 30 minutes of actual knowledge that a resident is missing (Mattie's Call Act).
Report the start and end of a Mattie's Call to DCH within 30 minutes of the contact with law enforcement (111-8-63-.30(1)).
Elopement-risk identification, door alarms and search procedures: Rule .18 body text was not retrieved. Review it before finalizing.
Do not lock residents into or out of rooms or restrict common areas (.17(7)).
Keep a current photo and description for each at-risk resident.

policies.category: Safety and Protection
policies.title: Restraints and Restrictive Practices
state_specifics: Do not admit or retain residents who need physical or chemical restraints, isolation or confinement for behavioral control (111-8-63-.15(1)).
Rule .03 counts bedrails, wheelchair safety bars, tight tucking and mitts as restraints. Alarm wristbands do not count.
Do not lock a resident into or out of the bedroom (.17(7)).
Assistive devices need an order, a written care plan and resident consent (.03).
Staff training on alternatives to restraint.

policies.category: Safety and Protection
policies.title: Fire Safety, Physical Plant Safety and Electrical Compliance
state_specifics: State Fire Marshal report with no violations and the capacity load, dated within 12 months of application.
Electrical compliance form signed by a Georgia-licensed electrician, dated within 6 months of application.
Keep the interior and exterior clean, in good repair and free of unsafe conditions. Keep entrances, exits, sidewalks and escape routes clear (111-8-63-.13).
Name and house number visible from the street (.13).
Maintain a drill and fire equipment inspection log.

policies.category: Daily Living
policies.title: Food Service, Menus and Therapeutic Diets
state_specifics: At least 3 regularly scheduled well-balanced meals a day, 7 days a week, plus therapeutic diets as ordered (111-8-63-.21).
No more than 14 hours between the evening and morning meals. Offer at least one nutritious snack daily.
Menus dated and planned at least 1 week ahead for regular and therapeutic diets. Post or make them easily available and encourage resident input.
Hold perishables at or below 41 degrees F.
Food must be clean, wholesome and safe. Keep menus as served for the period the current rule requires (a third-party copy says 30 days).

policies.category: Daily Living
policies.title: Activities, Social Programming and Transportation
state_specifics: Provide daily social activities (111-8-63-.17(4)).
Residents choose activities and schedules (.25).
The admission agreement sets transportation provisions, with emergency transport available at all times (.16).
Memory care activity program described in the profile (.19).
Keep an activity calendar and participation log.

policies.category: Daily Living
policies.title: Housekeeping, Laundry, Furnishings and Maintenance
state_specifics: Furnishings kept intact and functional. Name plate outside each room unless declined (111-8-63-.12).
Individual bed at least 36 x 72 inches. Mattress at least 5 inches thick (4 if synthetic). No cots, roll-aways, double-decks, stacked bunks, hide-a-beds or studio couches.
Closet or wardrobe and reading-adequate lighting in each room.
Linens for residents needing linen service: at least 2 sheets, pillow, pillowcase, blanket, bedspread, towels and washcloth.
Interior and exterior kept clean and in good repair (.13). Indoor temperature standards are in Rule .22 (body text not retrieved).

policies.category: Staffing and Personnel
policies.title: Background Checks, Registries and Fingerprint Determinations
state_specifics: Criminal background checks under Ch. 111-8-12 (111-8-63-.09(11)-(13)). GCHEXS fingerprint check for administrators and owners with 10%+; determination letter dated within 12 months.
The administrator needs a satisfactory determination before serving. GCHEXS support: 404-463-7154, gchexs.user@dch.ga.gov.
Check the Georgia Certified Medication Aide Registry for CMAs (.20).
An owner, director or employee acquiring a criminal record is reported to DCH within 24 hours (.30).
Document the check, the date and the outcome in the personnel file.

policies.category: Staffing and Personnel
policies.title: Hiring, Orientation, Employee Health and Personnel Records
state_specifics: Obtain employment history (111-8-63-.09(14)-(15)). Keep personnel files for 3 years after departure.
TB screening and physical within 12 months before providing care (.09(10)).
Ages: on-site manager and responsible staff 21+; no hands-on staff under 18 without line-of-sight supervision (.09(1)).
Orientation and training within 60 days; track CE hours (24 in year one, 16 per year after).
Staff wear ID badges (.09(22)). Keep staffing plans and schedules 1 year (.09(21)).

policies.category: Records
policies.title: Resident Records and Retention
state_specifics: The administrator or on-site manager keeps an individual file for each resident (111-8-63-.24).

Contents: identification; physician, hospital and pharmacy of choice; monetary transactions with itemized receipts; valuables receipts and inventory; health information; signed Resident's Rights form; signed admission agreement; powers of attorney; advance directives; signed end-of-life medical orders.
Files are available for inspection by DCH, and for inspection and copying by the resident or representative.
Investigation copies go in the resident file and the central QA file (.26).
Set a record retention period with counsel; no resident-file retention period was confirmed in the retrieved text.

policies.category: Records
policies.title: Required Reports to DCH
state_specifics: Within 24 hours: unanticipated or accidental death, serious injury needing medical attention, rape, assault, battery, abuse, neglect or exploitation, external disaster affecting safe operation, an owner, director or employee acquiring a criminal record (111-8-63-.30).
Within 30 minutes: Mattie's Call start and end.
Plan of correction within 10 days of receipt of the inspection report (.10).
Keep DCH supplied with current contacts (pchprogram.hfrd@dch.ga.gov) and keep the residential care profile accurate.
Report contents: names, dates, incident type and description, immediate action.

policies.category: Medicaid Waiver Participation
policies.title: Medicaid Elderly and Disabled Waiver (CCSP/SOURCE ALS), EVV and Billing Integrity
state_specifics: Alternative Living Services covers 24-hour supervision in licensed PCHs. Waivers do not pay room and board. Secondary sources give a resident room-and-board payment of $768/month and $226 personal needs, effective 1/1/2026; confirm with DHS.
Enroll through GAMMIS before billing. Retroactive enrollment is not permitted, and revalidation is required.

EVV: Netsmart Mobile Caregiver+; personal support services under HCPCS T1019; applicable claims with dates of service on or after Sept 14, 2026 must use EVV. Whether it applies to the ALS service itself is unverified, so confirm with DCH.
Waiver entry starts with an Area Agency on Aging assessment (866-552-4464). DFCS determines financial eligibility.
CMS lists the waiver as expiring 11/08/2027. Bill only for documented services and keep records for audits.

forms.name: Resident's Rights Acknowledgment
forms.purpose: Signed Resident's Rights form kept in the resident file

forms.name: Admission Agreement and Rate/Fee Schedule
forms.purpose: Plain-language agreement stating fees, refunds, transportation and the complaint process

forms.name: Rate Increase Notice (30-day personal services / 60-day room and board)
Pre-Admission Screening and Sex Offender Registry Check
Physician Examination/Report (DCH form)
forms.purpose: Medical clearance, TB status and orders at admission

forms.name: Resident Needs Assessment and Reassessment
forms.purpose: ADL, cognitive, behavioral and preference assessment

forms.name: Written Care Plan (within 14 days, annual update)
Medication Administration Record (MAR) and Controlled Substance Log
CMA Registry Check and Competency Checklist
forms.purpose: Medication aide verification, quarterly observation and annual review

forms.name: Incident/Accident Investigation Report

documents.title: Rule 111-8-63-.07 Owner Governance, paragraph (2). This is the list of required policies and procedures for Assisted Living Communities (25+ residents).
documents.issuer: Georgia Department of Community Health, Healthcare Facility Regulation Division (HFRD). Published by the Georgia Secretary of State, Rules & Regulations.
documents.version: Current text posted at rules.sos.ga.gov (Subject 111-8-63), fetched 10/14/2026. The page shows no effective date for .07.
documents.how_used: Main source for ALC policy content. .07(2) says the governing body must implement policies, procedures and practices that support dignity, respect, choice, independence and privacy in a safe environment. It also says the policies must, at a minimum, give direction to staff and residents on items (a) through (p). Georgia has no separate DCH policy checklist form, so this regulation section is the list.

documents.title: Rule 111-8-62-.07 Governing Body, paragraph (3). This is the list of required policies and procedures for Personal Care Homes (2–24 beds).
documents.issuer: Georgia Department of Community Health, Healthcare Facility Regulation Division (HFRD). Published by the Georgia Secretary of State, Rules & Regulations.
documents.version: Current text posted at rules.sos.ga.gov (Subject 111-8-62), fetched 10/14/2026. The page shows no effective date for .07.
documents.how_used: Main source for PCH policy content. .07(3) uses the same introductory language as the ALC rule and lists items (a) through (p). The PCH list is not identical to the ALC list: it has no separate rule items for ALC refunds order, staffing ratios for assisted self-preservation, or the ALC sub-list order. See the item text for the differences.

documents.how_used: This is the document the state uses at application. It does not list policy topics. Its 15 'Initial' items are all application paperwork and are excluded. It says all policies and procedures must be established under the regulations and be readily available on request. The notarized Affidavit of Compliance (Ch. 111-8-63) attests that the applicant has developed the mandated policies and procedures and will implement them immediately on licensure. The policy content is therefore taken from .07(2).

required_items.text: the services available in the assisted living community, including, personal services, assisted living care, memory care services and any other specialized services such as memory care centers and designated proxy caregivers;
the staffing plan that the community utilizes to ensure that staffing ratios increase proportionally as the number of residents who require assisted self-preservation increases;

admissions, discharges and immediate transfers which ensure that the community does not admit or retain residents who need more care that the assisted living community is authorized or capable of providing;
refunds when a resident is transferred or discharged;
training and ongoing evaluation of staff, including specialized training if designated proxy caregivers are provided or memory care is offered;
house rules and their enforcement;
protecting the rights of the residents as set forth in these rules;
medication management, procurement, the use of certified medication aides and professional oversight provided for such services;
health and hygiene issues for residents and staff relating to infection control, work policies and return to work policies, food borne illnesses and reportable diseases;

the investigation and reporting of abuse, neglect, exploitation of residents, residents' wandering away from the community, accidents, injuries and changes in residents' conditions to required parties;
discipline procedures for handling acts committed by staff which are inconsistent with the policies of the assisted living community;
emergency preparedness, drills and evacuation requirements;
quality assurance review mechanisms, including resident and family feedback to determine opportunities for improving care;
the use of volunteers and their orientation regarding resident's rights and basic safety precautions;

the specific use of proxy caregivers allowed within the community and the oversight of proxy caregivers the community requires or provides in accordance with Georgia law, these rules and the rules for proxy caregivers, Chapter 111-8-100; and

the safety and security precautions that will be employed by the assisted living community to protect residents from harm by other residents, designated proxy caregivers, and other individuals, not employed by the community who routinely come into the community.
The services available in the home, including, personal services, memory care services/centers and any other specialized services such as designated proxy caregivers.
Admissions, discharges and immediate transfers which ensure that the home does not admit or retain residents who need more care than the home is authorized or capable of providing.
Refunds when a resident is transferred or discharged.
Training and ongoing evaluation of staff, including specialized training if designated proxy caregivers are provided or memory care is offered.
House rules and their enforcement.
Protecting the rights of the residents as set forth in these rules;
Medication management, procurement and the professional oversight provided for such services.
Health and hygiene issues for residents and staff relating to infection control, work policies and return to work policies, food borne illnesses and reportable diseases.

The investigation and reporting of abuse, neglect, exploitation of residents, residents' wandering away from the community, accidents, injuries and changes in residents' conditions to required parties.
Discipline procedures for handling conduct which is inconsistent with the policies of the home committed by staff.
Emergency preparedness, drills and evacuation requirements.

Quality assurance and peer review mechanisms to determine opportunities for improving care utilizing information acquired from reports and investigations of serious incidents, including resident and family feedback.
The use of volunteers, who have unsupervised access to the residents and their orientation regarding resident's rights and basic safety precautions.

The specific use of proxy caregivers allowed within the home and the oversight of proxy caregivers the home requires or provides in accordance with Georgia law, these rules and the rules for proxy caregivers, Chapter 111-8-100.

The safety and security precautions that will be employed by the home to protect residents from harm by other residents, designated proxy caregivers and other individuals, not employed by the home who routinely come into the home.
The staffing plan which takes into account the specific needs of the residents and also includes arrangements for staffing in the absence of regularly scheduled staff.

sections: ALC: Rule 111-8-63-.07(2), policies and procedures (a) through (p), in the rule's order
PCH: Rule 111-8-62-.07(3), policies and procedures (a) through (p), in the rule's order

official.notes: No single DCH policy-review form exists for Georgia ALCs or PCHs, so the rule sections above are used instead. The rule lists the topics only as lettered paragraphs with no headings, so use the lettered items as the manual's categories. Section names are not invented. Use the ALC list for 25+ beds (Ch. 111-8-63) and the PCH list for 2–24 beds (Ch. 111-8-62). The two lists differ in order and wording: the ALC list adds the certified medication aide reference in (h) and orders its staffing-ratio item as (b), while the PCH list puts the staffing plan last as (p). Both rules say the lists are a 'minimum', so they are not exhaustive. Other sections of Chapters 111-8-62 and 111-8-63 contain further written-policy or program requirements, such as resident rights, memory care and staff training. I did not read those sections in this pass, so I did not list them. Check them before finalizing a manual. Submission and review: the HFRD checklists do not ask for the policies manual to be uploaded in the GAHLES portal. Their 'Initial' items are application paperwork only (14 for PCH, 15 for ALC). Instead, the applicant signs a notarized Affidavit of Compliance for the applicable chapter (111-8-63 or 111-8-62). It attests that the policies and procedures have been developed and will be implemented immediately once licensed. DCH says licensed facilities face unannounced periodic inspections where the policies must be 'readily available' for review for sufficiency and compliance. Deficient policies may bring sanctions under Ga. Comp. R. & Regs. 111-8-25. The checklists also say all policies and procedures must be established and readily available upon request. The manual should therefore be organized item by item so each lettered paragraph can be found quickly during a survey. Fetched 10/14/2026. The checklist pages carry no revision dates, so re-check the DCH page before relying on them. The fetched PCH rule text was cut off partway through .08, which does not affect .07(3).
